title: How to File a Consumer Complaint
summary: If a product or service fails you, the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 gives you a clear path to a refund or replacement.

body.text: If you buy a product or a service and it is defective, late, unsafe or not what was promised, you have rights. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 protects buyers in shops, online and over the phone.
Your main rights as a consumer

items: Right to be informed about quality, quantity and price.
Right to be heard and to seek redressal.
Right to seek compensation for unfair trade practices.

body.text: For e-commerce, the E-Commerce Rules, 2020 require sellers to display return, refund and warranty policies clearly before you buy.
How to complain, step by step
First complain to the seller in writing. If they do not fix it, you can approach a Consumer Commission.

items: District Commission: claims up to 50 lakh rupees.
State Commission: claims between 50 lakh and 2 crore rupees.
National Commission: claims above 2 crore rupees.

body.text: You usually have two years from the date of the problem to file a complaint.
You can file online through the e-Daakhil portal, and get guidance by calling the National Consumer Helpline 1915.

practicalSteps: Keep the bill, order ID, warranty card and all chats or emails.
Send a written complaint to the seller and note the date.
Call 1915 or register on consumerhelpline.gov.in for guidance.
File on the e-Daakhil portal if the seller does not resolve it.
exceptions: Products bought for resale or commercial use are generally not covered.
Free services given without any payment may fall outside the Act.
Some disputes must first go to a sector regulator, such as telecom or insurance.

faqs.a: Not necessarily. Consumer Commissions are designed to be simple, and you can argue your own case. Free help is available through consumer helplines and legal aid.

faqs.q: Can I complain about a service, not just a product?
faqs.a: Yes. The Act covers services such as banking, insurance, telecom, housing and repairs.

misconceptions.myth: Online sellers are not responsible because they are just a platform.
misconceptions.fact: The E-Commerce Rules, 2020 place duties on both the seller and the marketplace platform.
